title: role prompts carry the project's design from the engine side
acceptance: Implements design.md section 15.7. Worker and reviewer prompts carry, from the engine side: the role skill, the pinned spec, the project's design file at the pin's commit bounded in size with any truncation stated in the prompt, the project's base and its pinned T-043 contract (every field), and the absolute path of the checkpoint helper in the frozen code tree.

The worker and reviewer skills stop pointing at repository-relative files (design/design.md, design/tasks.json, bin/fm-checkpoint.sh) and refer to the design, scope and checkpoint command in the prompt; they stay portable English with no vendor-specific syntax. The firstmate skill says firstmate runs in the engine root and names --project on every script it calls, with one exception from design.md section 15.10 point 2: its routine dispatch step, after a green light and whenever a run ends, calls fm-dispatch.sh with no --project so free slots are filled fairly across every registered project, and it names --project for dispatch only when the captain asks for one project's work. The firstmate skill also says every card firstmate raises by hand takes the id fm-decide.sh --allocate gives it, D-<project>-<task>-<n> (design.md section 15.10 point 1), never a number picked by hand.
The self project's prompt has the same shape; the reviewer still receives the diff, the spec and the design and never the worker's reasoning (R2).
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
